Published online:
    2 September 2026

Geographic focus:
    Middle East (Qatar, UAE, Oman, Strait of Hormuz), Asia (India, Japan), Singapore

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — documents STS transfers occurring in July–August 2026
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ongoing Hormuz disruption, elevated LNG prices, continued supply rerouting
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Since a US-Israeli war on Iran broke out on February 28, 2026, the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut, severely disrupting LNG flows from Qatar and the UAE. In response, three LNG cargoes have been rerouted via ship-to-ship transfers outside the strait — an unusual practice for LNG. Vessels involved include GasLog Shanghai/Savannah (Qatar→Oman STS), Al Rekayyat/Tembek (Qatar→UAE coast STS, then delivered to India's Dahej), and Mraweh/LNG Enugu (UAE→Oman STS, en route to Japan). Asian spot LNG prices have surged to $23.20/mmBtu, more than double pre-conflict levels. The STS workaround reflects growing operational complexity and risk premium baked into regional LNG supply chains.
